title.narrative: ACF/NRC Food and nutrition security Cabo Delgado
ACF/NRC Livelihoods and food security Cabo Delgado

description.narrative: Insatsen uppgår till en summa av 65 000 000 SEK, med en aktivietsperiod som sträcker sig över tre år. Projektet kommer att inkludera aktiviteter för att återskapa människors försörjningsmöjligheter och öka den socio-ekonomiska motståndskraften, förbättra befolkningens tryggade livsmedelsförsörjning och nutrition och verka för förbättrad lokal kapacitet att reducera och hantera naturkatastrofrelaterade risker.

The contribution proposed will span over three years and 65 000 000 SEK, and will include work to recover people's lost livelihood opportunities and increase socio-economic resilience, improve food security and nutrition and seek to increase local capacities to reduce and manage risks associated with natural hazards.

The overall objective of the programme is to contribute to the creation of appropriate conditions to improve the lives of the rural population living in areas affected by conflict in the province of Cabo Delgado.
Nine communities, in which both IDPs and host populations are present, and in which long-term nexus programming is relevant and feasible, will be selected at the beginning of the intervention.
The programme will prioritise interventions within the food security and livelihoods sector, including activities focusing on water sanitation and hygiene, protection, and health (mainly nutrition). There will also be a disaster risk reduction component to the project for the improved management and reduction of disaster risks.
The specific goals are described below:
- Meet basic food security and livelihood needs of the most vulnerable communities and individuals and improve access to basic services and protection.
- Improve socio-economic resilience and improve food and nutrition security. Support the recovery of the production system, with good agronomic practices, and increase the diversification of livelihoods through providing access to alternative income sources.
- Support the recovery of critical services for the affected host communities and IDPs (markets, health centers, water and sanitation)
- Reduce disaster impact by strengthening local capacities in managing and mitigating disaster risks.
The project aims to reach 20 725 unique beneficiaries, where 15 508 are host community members (including returnees) and 5 217 are IDPs.

description.narrative:
Summary of Key Results Achieved
The Cabo Delgado Livelihoods and Food Security Programme has delivered important results in strengthening food security, livelihoods, community resilience, and local governance among conflict-affected populations in the districts of Mueda and Metuge. Despite operating in a highly challenging environment marked by insecurity, displacement, climate shocks, Cyclone Chido, drought, cholera outbreaks, and post-election unrest, the programme successfully maintained implementation and achieved tangible results through a community-led and resilience-focused approach.
1. Community Empowerment and Local Development The programme strengthened local governance and community ownership of development processes. Results achieved: - Established and strengthened 9 Community Action Plan (CAP) Committees involving 180 community members. - Developed and validated 9 Community Action Plans (5 in Mueda and 4 in Metuge).
The CAP process strengthened community participation, accountability, and collaboration with local authorities, creating locally owned development plans that will continue to guide future interventions beyond the project lifespan.
2. Food Security, Nutrition and Climate-Resilient Agriculture The programme improved household food production and resilience through climate-smart and nutrition-sensitive agricultural interventions. Results achieved: - 810 farmers supported through agricultural and livestock activities. - 135 lead farmers trained in Good Agricultural Practices, agroecology, post-harvest management, integrated pest management, irrigation, and livestock management. - 675 additional farmers supported (seeds, agricultural toolkits, cassava cuttings, irrigation equipment, livestock, and veterinary kits).
3. Livelihood Diversification and Economic Recovery The programme created new income-generating opportunities for vulnerable households, particularly women, youth, IDPs, and returnees. Results achieved: - 4,302 community members registered and assessed for livelihood support.. - 1,305 individuals pre-selected: 860 beneficiaries selected for Income Generating Activities (IGAs): 270 youth trained (entrepreneurship, market analysis, business planning, and legal aspects of business development): 261 IGAs funded.
4. Fisheries Livelihood Support The programme supported artisanal fishing communities to diversify livelihoods and strengthen food security. Results achieved: - 25 fisherfolk selected and trained in sustainable fishing practices. - Fishing kits distributed in the communities of Milamba and 25 de Junho.
5. Disaster Risk Reduction and Community Resilience The programme strengthened local capacities to prepare for and respond to disasters and climate-related shocks. Results achieved: - Established and strengthened 9 Community Disaster Risk Reduction Committees involving 162 members (60 women and 102 men): Provided smartphones to DRR committees to support early warning and emergency communication. - Developed local Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) plans. - Conducted climate adaptation and preparedness campaigns across all target communities. - Strengthened collaboration with INGD, INAM, SDAE, SPAE, and SDPI.
These interventions improved community preparedness and resilience to floods, droughts, cyclones, and other climate-related risks.
6. Community Infrastructure and Essential Services The programme supported investments in community infrastructure identified through the Community Action Plans and DRR processes. Results achieved: Construction and rehabilitation commenced for 7 priority infrastructures, including: Community markets; Bridge construction; Culvert construction; Dam rehabilitation; Borehole drilling and water supply systems.
These investments will improve market access, mobility, water availability, and climate resilience for target communities.
7. Legal Assistance and Access to Rights The programme integrated legal empowerment as a key component of resilience and sustainable development. Results achieved: - 4,302 community members reached through legal awareness and counselling activities. This support helped address legal barriers that often limit access to economic opportunities and essential services.
8. Emergency Response Following Cyclone Chido Following the impact of Cyclone Chido in December 2024, the programme rapidly activated its Crisis Modifier mechanism to protect livelihoods and support affected communities. Results achieved: More than 3,000 households received emergency support. - Agricultural recovery kits and replacement seeds distributed. - Shelter and hygiene kits provided to affected households. - Community rehabilitation and debris-clearing equipment distributed through local DRR committees. - Support provided for the rehabilitation of critical community infrastructure.
This rapid response helped prevent further deterioration of food security conditions and safeguarded investments already made by the programme.
Overall Achievement Overall, the programme has performed well and delivered substantial results despite the challenging operating environment. The consortium has demonstrated strong commitment and adaptability in achieving programme objectives and supporting vulnerable populations. Final results will be consolidated and validated during the programme closure phase, with a comprehensive assessment of achievements and outcomes to be provided in the final report due on 30 November 2026.
